correctness.rationale: An ordinary period p<n supplies a legal infinite repetition because the wrap transition already appears inside the prefix. For p=n the word is unbordered and its endpoints differ, again giving a legal repeat. Conversely an infinite periodic extension induces a word period no smaller than the least word period. Reversal pairs the two orientations of unbordered words. A shortest border is itself unbordered; if its length k exceeded n/2, the induced period n−k would restrict to a proper period of that border. Thus the disjoint shortest-border sandwich has middle count F_(n−2k+1), including one empty middle, and the total oriented count F_(n−1) yields the functional equation. For D(z)=1−z−z²=(1−z/q)(1+qz), the numerator q²−T(q²) is strictly positive since T(y)≤y²/(1−y−y²)<y at y=q². Hence the first pole at q has positive normalized principal coefficient A. Iterating the equation inside the disk gives simple poles at ±s for s=√q, with principal coefficients −A/(2D(±s)) because the root substitution divides the principal coefficient by two. Their even and odd sums, divided by A, are q/(1−q³) and 1/(√q(1−q³)). Subtract also the four simple parts at radius q^(1/4); the residual is analytic in a strictly larger disk, so the omitted coefficient is O(q^(−n/4)). Multiplying by the reciprocal Fibonacci count gives the claimed O(q^(3n/4)) remainder, as the conjugate Binet term has strictly faster exponential decay. Pole preimages cannot cancel: the inhomogeneous term is analytic and D is nonzero on every descendant shell. Dyadic pole accumulation then prohibits meromorphic extension anywhere on the unit circle. I directly tested finite periodic extensions through n=13 by generating each candidate repeating prefix and tested constants using a 300-degree recurrence; the frozen checks were inspected, not executed. The repair also corrects the checker description: there are 219 coefficient assertions in degrees 2 through 220.
residual_risks: The exact atom is for distinct indexed words under uniform finite-language sampling, not primitive orbits, morphic Fibonacci factors, or a Gibbs measure. Finite checks do not certify the infinite pole conclusions.
